chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qad-dah, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Be shy of God as He deserves. They asked, 'What should we do?' He said, 'If you do so, none of you will go to sleep without seeing your death with your own eyes. You should guard your mind and whatever goes on in it. You must guard your stomach and whatever goes into it. You should remember your grave and the fact that your body will spoil there. Whoever wants the Hereafter should abandon the adornments of the life of this world.'

key_terms.أَجَلُهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ: Death/deadline before one's eyes (constant awareness of death)
key_terms.الرَّأْسَ وَمَا وَعَى: The head and what it contains (the mind/intellect)
key_terms.حَقَّ الْحَيَاءِ: True shyness/modesty as deserving by God
key_terms.وَمَا حَوَى: And what it contains (referring to the stomach)

ai.seo_question: What are the practical actions required to achieve true shyness before God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal outlines the practical dimensions of 'true shyness' (ḥaqq al-ḥayāʾ) by linking internal mindfulness with external asceticism. Shaykh al-Ṣadūq presents it as a holistic spiritual discipline where guarding the 'container' of the head (intellect) and stomach (desires) serves as a constant reminder of mortality, thereby prioritizing the eternal Hereafter over transient worldly luxuries.
